title: Conditional acceptance lanes for phased PRD rollbacks and legal escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent PRDs that trimmed scope midway through implementation exposed ambiguity about when a partial delivery is 'acceptable' vs when teams must pause and roll back. This ticket creates deterministic, cross-team acceptance lanes for phased PRD rollbacks and legal escalation decisions so Engineering, Design, and Legal can sign off consistently.

Scope: Define a lightweight lane model (Green / Conditional / Red) with explicit guardrails, owner assignments, and artifact checklists. Produce sign-off templates, a short decision matrix based on risk categories (data residency, PII exposure, SLA regression, billing changes), and a rollout/rollback playbook that ties into existing canary and feature-flag processes. Deliverables include: sign-off template, Confluence runbook, CI gating checklist, and a one-page decision cheat sheet for on-call and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Lane definitions documented: Green (ship), Conditional (ship with mitigations), Red (block/rollback)
Owner mapped for each lane: ENG lead, Design lead, Legal reviewer, and PM owner
Sign-off template created and stored in Confluence with required artifact links (PRD, Figma, security checklist, telemetry dash)
Decision matrix with examples for common cases (KV cache changes, telemetry opt-ins, model fallback exposures)
CI gating checklist created and validated by ENG: automated tests + telemetry smoke check must pass for Green lanes
Rollback playbook validated in a tabletop exercise with on-call, engineering, and support
Legal escalation flow defined for data residency/contractual breaches and tested with Legal partner
Post-release monitoring dashboard template linked and a 72-hour monitoring runbook published
updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with ENG (Marcus Chen), Design (Priya Rao) and Legal (Diego Alvarez). Agreed on lane taxonomy but requested concrete examples and thresholds for SLA regressions.
2026-02-25: Draft sign-off template uploaded to Confluence (link below). Design requested an accessibility/UX checklist to be added for Conditional lanes.
2026-02-28: Engineering asked to clarify CI gating feasibility—ENG owner (Marcus) to prototype a lightweight smoke test that validates dependent model variants and telemetry emitters.
2026-03-03: Legal reviewed decision matrix and requested explicit criteria for when KMS/HSM changes trigger Red lane. Legal to provide a short checklist by 2026-03-08.

2026-03-06: Ran tabletop rollback exercise with on-call and SRE; found two missing runbook steps around cache invalidation and KV eviction order. Action: ENG to update playbook and add rollback checklist item.
2026-03-09: Design provided Figma flows for UI messaging during Conditional releases. Agreed to include a standardized banner copy and user-facing telemetry opt-out path.
2026-03-10: Consolidated artifacts, preparing for cross-team review session on 2026-03-12. Next: finalize sign-off template and publish runbook for org-wide use.
notes: Decision trade-offs: kept the lane model intentionally simple (3 lanes) to avoid heavy ceremony for small scope trims.

Engineering trade-off: CI gating will start as advisory for the first two quarters to avoid blocking iterative work; will be promoted to mandatory for Green lanes after telemetry coverage reaches 85%.
Legal note: any change that affects encryption, contract terms, or cross-border data handling auto-escalates to Red unless mitigations approved in writing.
Design note: user-facing messaging must be reviewed for localization and accessibility; plan includes translation pass and voiceover for major markets.
Action items: Marcus to prototype smoke test by 2026-03-16; Diego to deliver legal checklist by 2026-03-08; Priya to finalize banner copy by 2026-03-14.
